reason: E1 directly supports the competition between ΔHmix and TΔSmix governing phase selection and stability, which is the core premise. E2 and E3 provide general evidence for high-temperature strength and thermal stability of HEAs, but do not specifically address premelting/melting behavior or the mechanistic link to ΔHmix/TΔSmix in nanoparticles. The premises about nanoparticle suitability and thermal stability are only loosely tied to the cited passages.
premises: Phase selection in high-entropy materials is determined by competition between ΔHmix and TΔSmix
Entropy stabilization occurs when TΔSmix balances or exceeds ΔHmix
More negative ΔGmix indicates increased stability from higher configurational entropy
High-entropy alloys exhibit thermal stability at high temperatures
Nanoparticles of high-entropy alloys are suitable for high-temperature applications
